name: Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome

criteria.description: Fasting serum gastrin > 10 times upper limit of normal (> 1000 pg/mL) with gastric pH < 2
Positive secretin stimulation test (gastrin increase > 120 pg/mL after IV secretin)
Imaging identification of gastrinoma (CT, MRI, EUS, or somatostatin receptor scintigraphy)
Association with MEN1 syndrome (present in 20-30% of ZES cases)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Fasting hypergastrinemia with gastric acid hypersecretion (pH < 2) plus either positive secretin stimulation test or localization of gastrinoma on imaging. PPIs must be held before testing.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: 60-90% of gastrinomas are malignant. 70-80% are in the gastrinoma triangle (duodenum > pancreas). 20-30% are associated with MEN1.

pathognomonic.notes: Ulcers often in atypical locations (distal duodenum, jejunum), multiple, or refractory to standard therapy

common.notes: Secretory diarrhea from gastric acid hypersecretion; may be sole presenting symptom in 10-20%

rare.symptomName: Hepatic metastases causing right upper quadrant pain
rare.notes: Liver metastases present in 25% at diagnosis

laboratory: Fasting serum gastrin markedly elevated (often > 1000 pg/mL; normal < 100)
Gastric pH < 2 (confirms acid hypersecretion; rules out achlorhydria as cause of hypergastrinemia)
Positive secretin stimulation test (gastrin rise > 120 pg/mL)
Serum calcium and PTH to screen for MEN1-associated hyperparathyroidism
imaging: CT/MRI abdomen: may demonstrate pancreatic or duodenal mass; liver metastases
Somatostatin receptor scintigraphy (OctreoScan): sensitivity ~80% for localization
Ga-68 DOTATATE PET/CT: superior sensitivity for gastrinoma localization
EUS: high sensitivity for small pancreatic and duodenal gastrinomas
genetic: MEN1 gene mutations (chromosome 11q13) in MEN1-associated cases (20-30%)
Genetic testing for MEN1 recommended in all ZES patients
other: Gastric pH measurement (must be < 2 while off PPIs to interpret gastrin levels)
Basal acid output > 15 mEq/h (or > 5 mEq/h in post-vagotomy patients)
Upper endoscopy: prominent gastric folds, multiple ulcers, ulcers beyond first duodenum

distinguishingFeatures: Typical PUD has normal gastrin levels
PUD responds to standard PPI therapy
Usually single ulcer in typical location
PPI use causes compensatory hypergastrinemia with high gastric pH
G-cell hyperplasia from chronic atrophic gastritis has high pH

redFlags: Multiple ulcers in atypical locations (post-bulbar, jejunal)
Peptic ulcer disease refractory to standard PPI therapy
Diarrhea that resolves with PPI therapy (suggests acid-mediated mechanism)
Family history of MEN1 features (hyperparathyroidism, pituitary tumors)
references: Jensen RT, et al. Zollinger-Ellison syndrome: current concepts and management. Ann Surg. 2023;277(2):197-215.
Ito T, et al. Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: clinical features, diagnosis and medical treatment advances. Best Pract Res Clin Gastroenterol. 2012;26(6):737-753.
Zollinger RM, Ellison EH. Primary peptic ulceration of the jejunum associated with islet cell tumors of the pancreas. Ann Surg. 1955;142(4):709-723.
